bear_case: There is no buyer. The user is real (drone operators, S2 cells, wildfire IMTs on ATAK) but the chain breaks immediately above them: no requirement owner names drone-agnostic sensor-to-map or bandwidth-budgeted terrain distribution, no program office owns it (TPC owns the client roadmap, AGC owns basemap packaging, DHS S&T owns the first-responder TAK program, PM IS&A owns Army edge exploitation via AIDP-Next), no contracting office buys plugins, and no budget line exists - the card itself records 'Public evidence insufficient'. Where money exists it is prime-shaped (AIDP-Next single award, TITAN production, NGC2 OTAs led by Anduril) or program-internal (DHS S&T paying integrators). Worse, the public-safety segment the parent skeptics pointed to has already revealed its price: agencies are adopting a fully free stack (ATAK + UAS Tool + MediaMTX) for drone video, and the KLV footprint overlay they get from it is the first function in this gap's title. The residual pains - change judged by eye, stale terrain packages - remained HYPOTHESIS/LOW after G03's two passes and this third pass found no AAR, solicitation or SOP naming them. The closest funded analogs (Reveal via STRATFI; Immersive Wisdom via a $25M-ceiling ordering contract; TAK services houses) are either SBIR-gated, which the cap table cannot pass today, or services-priced, which is consultancy drift by definition.
strongest_single_argument: The government already owns the vendor-neutral, free layer this gap proposes to sell (TAK, UAS Tool, AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles, TAK Server sync), so the natural requirement owner is also the incumbent supplier; there is no office whose job is to buy this from a third party, and the public-safety buyer has shown it expects the footprint feature for free.

what_would_change_my_mind: A primary source (SAM.gov solicitation, DHS S&T BAA, state TAK program RFP, unit AAR or SOP) naming edge change-vs-baseline overlays or bandwidth-prioritised distribution of 3D terrain/basemap packages as a distinct paid requirement; or evidence that a state/agency TAK program or allied civil-protection agency has paid a third party a recurring fee for a sensor-to-map plugin rather than obtaining it through TPC or a services contract.
narrower_survivable_version: None as a company. A bootstrapped, open-source ATAK-CIV change-overlay plugin used as a demand probe (3 months, under $30k) with paid support from one state TAK program or allied civil-protection agency as the only revenue model; exit by acqui-hire into Reveal, Skydio or a TAK integrator.

bear_case: Read the title against the market: 'MISB KLV to georegistered footprints' is the government's free UAS Tool plugin, confirmed this session from the user manual and Play listing; 'incremental 3D on a commodity edge box' is Skydio Onboard Modeling (a mesh on the controller within minutes, ATAK streaming offline, on the Army's company-level drone) and Reveal Farsight (2D/3D 'in mere moments' at the tactical edge, import/export to ATAK, developed with USSOCOM, $33.6M STRATFI, Maxar basemap/3D partnership May 2025, $30M Series B earmarked partly for acquisitions); '3D Tiles in TAK' is a TPC program with a Cesium update on the TAK Offsite 2026 agenda; the basemap packages are AGC's Releasable Basemap Tiles with an OGC standard in progress; the algorithms are OpenDroneMap and Obj2Tiles; the public-safety video-to-TAK channel is DroneSense, DJI-class platforms and Vision2; and the distribution half is TAK Server mission sync, CloudTAK package sync, the community map-depot plugin and Ditto's mission-ready Edge Sync. Every interface the startup would build on (TAK SDK, MIL plugin approval, basemap format, 3D Tiles rendering, KLV emission) is controlled by TPC, AGC, Cesium or the drone vendor. Government-owned software covers the vendor-neutral position outright, so Anduril/Palantir/L3Harris do not even need to respond. The two residual increments - change-vs-baseline overlays at the edge and priority-scheduled delta of 3D terrain - are one or two release cycles away for TPC, Reveal, Skydio or Ditto (INFERENCE, MEDIUM), and a startup's switching cost is nil because its output is standard tiles and CoT that any of them can also emit.
strongest_single_argument: The gap's first function is a free government plugin and its second is a stock feature of the Army's chosen drone and the shipping product of a USSOCOM-born, $30M-Series-B, acquisitive competitor that already exports to ATAK - the startup would enter as the fourth supplier of a capability whose price is already zero.

what_would_change_my_mind: Written confirmation from TPC that change-vs-baseline overlays and bandwidth-budgeted priority delta of 3D terrain are out of scope for ATAK/TAK Server; a Reveal or Skydio public roadmap statement excluding change detection; and a documented case of a third-party TAK plugin vendor sustaining recurring licence revenue against the free baseline in a comparable function.
narrower_survivable_version: Only the change-vs-baseline overlay as an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin that consumes whatever 3D the user already has (Skydio, Reveal, ODM) - positioned explicitly as a complement to incumbents and a path to being acquired by one, not as a competitor to any of them.

bear_case: This scope was engineered to pass the feasibility lens, and it largely does: the MVP is unclassified by construction, uses open terrain and self-flown KLV video, runs on a Jetson and ATAK-CIV public source, is likely commercial software (EAR99 or 5D002/ENC - counsel to confirm), needs no ATO for agency-run pilots, and fits inside $250k with a 3-6 month demo. The Indonesian founder can engineer all of it. The refutation is therefore not 'cannot build' but 'cannot reach a fundable milestone with this team': three fatal-if-absent roles are missing (photogrammetry/SLAM engineer, TAK ecosystem engineer with TPC relationships, public-safety or SOF domain seller), the credible-demo milestone requires a sponsor for a live pilot the founders do not have, and the moment the product touches defense - TAK-GOV/MIL builds, CUI/OWT data, an xTech-to-SBIR path - the constraints return: 13 CFR 121.702 ownership/control test (Indonesian equity never counts; German equity only after permanent residency), AFWERX foreign-national limits on award work, TAK-MIL distribution control for the non-U.S.-person founder, and eventual FOCI review. None of these is fatal in the civil-only form, which is exactly why the civil-only form is also the form with no buyer. Capital is adequate for the PoC and inadequate for the 12-24 months of customer discovery needed to find a paying user inside a free ecosystem.
strongest_single_argument: The version of this gap that this team can legally and cheaply build is the version with no paying customer, and the version with a plausible defense customer is the version the team cannot enter without restructuring the cap table, waiting on a green card and hiring three specialists it cannot afford on $250k.

what_would_change_my_mind: A signed, paid pilot from a state TAK program, DHS S&T or an allied civil-protection agency for the civil-only plugin within six months of release (proving a buyer exists in the form this team can build); or counsel-confirmed SBIR eligibility for a restructured cap table plus a committed U.S.-person photogrammetry co-founder, which would reopen the defense variant.
narrower_survivable_version: Civil-only, open-source ATAK-CIV change-overlay plugin plus optional Jetson service, sold as paid support/hosting to public-safety TAK programs and allied civil-protection agencies, with no defense variant until the cap table, permanent residency and a U.S.-person technical hire are in place - run as a bootstrapped demand probe, not a venture.
